commentary: The liquidity hierarchy splits into three clear tiers. Nasdaq 100 and NYSE dominate with minimal price impact (0.0024% and 0.0058% per $1M traded respectively) and exceptional comparable volumes ($340.5M and $198.7M), establishing a US-equity anchor. The mid-tier—Tokyo Stock Exchange, Euronext, Hong Kong Stock Exchange, and London Stock Exchange—exhibits moderate price impact (0.0281% to 0.0362% per $1M) but diverges sharply on turnover: TSX shows robust 3.0065% turnover despite lower comparable volume ($54.1M), while Euronext and Hong Kong manage just 0.4388% and 0.4311% respectively on minimal activity ($11.0M and $12.1M). The laggard tier comprises Xetra, SIX Swiss Exchange, and Korea Exchange, where elevated ILLIQ values (0.0492% to 0.1577% per $1M) and wide spreads (0.5678% to 1.5545%) signal structural constraints. Korea Exchange stands apart as the outlier: despite ranking ninth in ILLIQ, its 1.5545% AR spread is substantially wider than peers, suggesting intraday volatility or order-book fragmentation that the price-impact metric alone fails to capture—a critical warning for execution desks targeting that market.
